findings.reason: prose ordering is not what the queue reads, so the very collision the sentence warns about is left possible.
findings.text: §6 says it "runs after §2, which also writes dispatch_batch.py", but the plan declares no `plan-section-depends-on` (the house convention used by e.g. docs/plans/a-finished-plan-closes.html) and every section's `data-links` is empty, so the dispatch queue sees no ordering and two nodes can hold a write scope over `reckon/crew/dispatch_batch.py` at once

findings.reason: the node's measure fails on the correct implementation, so a worker either weakens or drops the only check that the batch path matches the single-dispatch contract, and the plan should name the run id both sides use (or compare against the stored request's own run directory).
findings.text: §6's done-when requires the stored manifest path to equal the one "a single queued dispatch of the same node names", but that path is `runs_dir()/<run_id>/manifest.md` (dispatch_plan.py:823), so a batch entry and a single dispatch of the same node carry different run ids and can never name equal paths

findings.reason: the operative condition (provably gone by `local_liveness`, unprovable counted as a claim) survives the duplication and the surrounding done-when cases pin the behaviour, so an implementer reaches the same mechanism; it is a copy defect that should be fixed in place.
findings.text: §5's deliverable reads "starting and the other unlaunched claim phases count as a claim unless the worker is provably gone or its worker is provably gone by `local_liveness`", stating the escape twice with and without the predicate that proves it

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `WAITING_REQUEST_PHASES` (node.py:1569), `_UNLAUNCHED_CLAIM_PHASES` (dispatch_claims.py:120), `_live_pointer_worktrees` and its same-run skip (routing.py:1078/1092), `_launch_tree_verdict` (2173), `_remove_worktree` (2278), the launch pointer write (`"worktree"` at dispatch.py:2946, `"phase": "starting"` at 2991), `local_liveness` (recovery_liveness.py:1204), `_queue_batch` (dispatch_batch.py:502) and `plan-after`'s target all resolve.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §6's equality measure ("a manifest path equal to the one a single queued dispatch of the same node names") cannot hold as written, because the default manifest is run-scoped.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — every gate writes a test under `tests/` and §5's evidence note sits under the reports directory; no section names a scratchpad or node-local path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §6's deliverable and test name describe the capability; no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag reaches a symbol, filename or comment.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §5's deliverable sentence carries a duplicated condition, so the escape it states is written twice in two forms and the sentence no longer parses.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — each of the three reviewed units carries one deliverable; §2/§6's shared file is an ordering fact, not a second deliverable, and §6 hands the `1h30m` budget refusal explicitly to §2.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §6 depends on §2 landing first because both write `reckon/crew/dispatch_batch.py`, yet the plan declares no `plan-section-depends-on` and the ordering appears only as prose at the end of §6.
